topics.title: Introduction to Material Cost & Material Control
explain: Material cost is the cost of commodities or physical objects used to manufacture a final product.
Direct materials can be directly attributed to a specific end product in an economically feasible way.
Indirect materials cannot be directly assigned to a specific final product (e.g. lubricants, cleaning rags).
Material control applies the 3Es: Economy in procurement, Efficiency in handling, and Effectiveness in output.
Key objectives include avoiding production delays, optimizing material costs, and eliminating unnecessary waste.

flow.title: Material Control Objectives Flow
steps: Identify material requirements
Apply 3Es in procurement
Minimize storage and ordering costs
Maintain continuous production flow
Prevent wastage and pilferage

topics.example: A furniture maker uses wood as a direct material and sand paper or machinery grease as indirect materials.
remember: Direct materials physically form part of the final product and are easily traceable.
The 3Es stand for Economy, Efficiency, and Effectiveness.
mistakes: Treating low-cost items like glue or thread as direct materials when tracing them is not economically feasible.

quiz.q: Which of the following is classified as a direct material?
o: Cleaning spray used in the workshop
quiz.why: Timber is directly traceable to the chair and forms a major physical component of the product.

quiz.q: What do the 3Es of material control stand for?
quiz.why: Material control focuses on Economy in buying, Efficiency in handling, and Effectiveness in output.

topics.title: Materials Procurement Procedure & Documentation
explain: Procurement begins when user departments or storekeepers issue a Purchase Requisition.
Bill of Materials (BOM) is a master specification schedule listing all standard raw materials needed for a job.
Material Requisition Note (MRN) is an authorization slip to draw materials from the storehouse for production.
Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is an online portal used by public sector entities for transparent procurement.
Received materials are inspected, logged in a Goods Received Note (GRN), or returned via Material Returned Note.

flow.title: Procurement Sequence
steps: Prepare Bill of Materials
Originate Purchase Requisition
Invite Quotations or Tenders
Issue Purchase Order to supplier
Receive and inspect goods
Prepare Goods Received Note

topics.example: Before manufacturing 500 bicycles, the planning team prepares a BOM detailing frame, wheels, and chains required.
remember: BOM is prepared by planning/engineering as a master standard schedule.
MRN authorizes the physical release of stored material to production.
mistakes: Confusing BOM with MRN; BOM is a complete planning list, whereas MRN is an actual store withdrawal slip.

quiz.q: Which document acts as a voucher of authority to get materials issued from stores?
quiz.why: Material Requisition Note authorizes the storekeeper to issue materials to the consuming department.

quiz.q: Who originates a Purchase Requisition for regular stock items?
o: Storekeeper when stock reaches re-order level
Sales Manager after taking customer orders
quiz.why: The storekeeper prepares a purchase requisition when stock of regular inventory hits the re-order level.

topics.title: Valuation of Material Receipts
explain: Cost of material receipt includes purchase price, freight inwards, custom duty, insurance, and non-refundable taxes.
Trade discounts and quantity discounts are deducted directly from the purchase price.
Cash discounts are financing items for prompt payment and are NOT deducted from material purchase cost.
Goods and Services Tax (GST) is excluded from material cost if Input Tax Credit (ITC) is available.
Abnormal penalties such as demurrage and detention charges are excluded from material purchase cost.
Non-returnable container costs are added; refunds on returnable containers reduce the total purchase cost.

flow.title: Receipt Valuation Flow
steps: Start with gross invoice price
Deduct trade and quantity discounts
Add freight insurance and custom duty
Exclude GST if credit available
Add cost of non-returnable containers
Arrive at net cost of materials

topics.example: Buying steel for Rs 100,000 with 10% trade discount and Rs 5,000 freight makes net purchase cost Rs 95,000.
remember: Deduct Trade and Quantity discounts.
Ignore Cash discounts in cost accounting.
Exclude GST whenever Input Tax Credit is claimed.
mistakes: Deducting cash discounts from the cost of materials purchased.

quiz.q: How is a cash discount treated when determining the cost of material receipts?
o: Ignored as it is a finance item
quiz.why: Cash discount is an interest/finance item for early payment and is not deducted from material cost.

quiz.q: Demurrage paid to a transport company for delay in unloading is:
o: Excluded from material cost as abnormal loss
quiz.why: Demurrage is a penalty for delay, making it an abnormal cost charged directly to Costing P&L.

topics.title: Material Storage & Store Records
explain: The storekeeper maintains safe custody of inventory and ensures materials are available without interruption.
Bin Card is a quantitative record attached to each bin/rack in the store, maintained by the storekeeper.
Stock Control Card is a quantitative summary record maintained by the stores department for overall stock.
Stores Ledger records BOTH quantity and financial value, maintained independently by the Cost/Accounts department.
Bin Cards are posted physically at the exact moment of transaction; Stores Ledger is posted later from source documents.

flow.title: Store Record Maintenance
steps: Material arrives at store room
Update Bin Card quantity instantly
Send Goods Received Note to Accounts
Cost Dept posts quantity and value in Ledger
Periodically reconcile Bin Card with Ledger

topics.example: When 50 iron rods arrive, the storekeeper logs '+50' on the bin card tag; Costing logs 50 units @ Rs 200 in Stores Ledger.
remember: Bin Card = Quantity only (Store Keeper).
Stores Ledger = Quantity AND Value (Costing Dept).
mistakes: Assuming Bin Cards record unit price or monetary value of stocks.

quiz.q: Which store record tracks both quantitative details and monetary values of inventory?
quiz.why: Stores Ledger is maintained by the Cost Accounting department to track both physical quantity and money value.

quiz.q: Entries in Bin Cards are recorded:
o: At the end of the financial year
Simultaneously when goods are received or issued
Only when physical stock verification fails
quiz.why: Bin Card entries are made on the spot by the person physically handling the material receipt or issue.

topics.title: Inventory Control - Stock Levels & EOQ
explain: Re-order Level (ROL) = Maximum Consumption × Maximum Re-order Period. Alternatively, Min Level + (Avg Consumption × Avg Lead Time).
Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) minimizes total ordering and carrying costs: EOQ = √((2 × A × O) / C).
Maximum Stock Level = ROL + ROQ - (Minimum Consumption × Minimum Re-order Period).
Minimum Stock Level = ROL - (Average Consumption × Average Re-order Period).
Danger Level = Average Consumption × Emergency Purchase Lead Time.
Safety/Buffer Stock is extra reserve stock held to cushion against sudden demand spikes or supply delays.

flow.title: Stock Level Determination Sequence
steps: Determine consumption rates and lead times
Calculate Re-order Level (ROL)
Calculate EOQ to set order quantity
Establish Maximum and Minimum limits
Monitor Danger Level for emergency buys

topics.example: If annual demand is 10,000 units, order cost is Rs 50, carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit, EOQ = √((2×10000×50)/4) = 500 units.
remember: ROL = Max Usage × Max Lead Time.
EOQ formula: √((2AO)/C).
At EOQ, Total Annual Ordering Cost EQUALS Total Annual Carrying Cost.
mistakes: Using weekly usage with an annual carrying cost without keeping time units consistent.

quiz.q: At the Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), which condition holds true?
o: Total ordering cost equals total carrying cost
Purchase price per unit is minimum
quiz.why: EOQ is the point where annual ordering cost exactly equals annual carrying cost, minimizing total inventory cost.

quiz.q: What is the primary formula for Re-order Stock Level (ROL)?
quiz.why: ROL is set using maximum consumption and maximum lead time to ensure stock does not run out before fresh goods arrive.

topics.title: Selective Inventory Control & Ratio Analysis
explain: ABC Analysis classifies inventory by value: Category A (10% items, 70% value), B (20% items, 20% value), C (70% items, 10% value).
FSN Analysis categorizes inventory based on movement frequency: Fast-moving, Slow-moving, and Non-moving.
VED Analysis classifies spare parts by operational criticality: Vital, Essential, and Desirable.
HML Analysis categorizes inventory based on unit purchase price: High cost, Medium cost, and Low cost.
Inventory Turnover Ratio (ITR) = Cost of Materials Consumed / Average Stock. Higher ITR indicates fast-moving stock.
Average Inventory Holding Period = 365 days (or 12 months) / Inventory Turnover Ratio.

flow.title: ABC Inventory Classification
steps: List all inventory items
Calculate total annual expenditure per item
Rank items by annual monetary value
Assign top 70% value items to Category A
Assign next 20% value items to Category B
Assign remaining 10% value to Category C

topics.example: High-cost turbine blades are Category A (tight control), while cheap washers and bolts are Category C (simple bulk control).
remember: ABC is based on monetary investment value.
Higher Inventory Turnover Ratio = Fast moving material (less locked-up capital).
mistakes: Thinking Category A items constitute 70% of physical volume rather than 70% of monetary value.

quiz.q: VED analysis is primarily used for controlling which type of inventory?
o: Spare parts based on operational criticality
quiz.why: VED (Vital, Essential, Desirable) evaluates spare parts based on how severe a machine shutdown would be if unavailable.

quiz.q: A low Inventory Turnover Ratio indicates:
o: Over-investment and locked-up capital in inventory
quiz.why: A low turnover ratio means inventory stays unused for long periods, locking up working capital.

topics.title: Physical Control & Just-In-Time (JIT) System
explain: Just-In-Time (JIT) is a demand-pull management approach aimed at maintaining near-zero stock in stores.
Under JIT, raw materials are purchased and received only when required for immediate production.
Two Bin System splits storage into a main operational bin and an emergency reserve bin to signal re-ordering.
Perpetual Inventory System combines continuous record-keeping (Bin Cards & Stores Ledger) with continuous physical stock checks.
Continuous Stock Verification audits physical stock daily by rotation, avoiding factory shutdowns required by annual stocktaking.

flow.title: JIT Production Sequence
steps: Receive customer order for final product
Initiate production process
Send raw material requirement to purchase
Issue purchase order to supplier
Supplier delivers materials directly to line

topics.example: A car maker orders tires to arrive at the assembly plant just 2 hours before the car is built on the line.
remember: JIT operates on a demand-pull principle.
Continuous stock verification uses surprise physical counts throughout the year.
mistakes: Confusing perpetual inventory system with simple annual physical stock-taking.

quiz.q: What is the primary goal of Just-In-Time (JIT) inventory management?
o: Achieving zero or minimal inventory levels
quiz.why: JIT aims to eliminate inventory holding costs by receiving materials only when needed for production.

quiz.q: Which physical control system uses a smaller compartment of a storage box to signal re-ordering?
quiz.why: In the Two Bin System, drawing items from the second smaller bin triggers a fresh purchase order.

topics.title: Issue Procedure & Cost/Average Pricing Methods
explain: Materials are issued from stores against authorized Material Requisition Notes.
Material Transfer Note records direct transfer of surplus material from one job to another.
Shop Credit Note (Stores Debit Note) records return of unused surplus material from production back to stores.
FIFO (First-In, First-Out): Earliest bought lots are issued first. Closing stock reflects current market prices.
LIFO (Last-In, First-Out): Latest bought lots are issued first. Matches current cost with revenue, but NOT permitted by AS 2.
Weighted Average Price Method recalculates unit issue price after every fresh receipt: Total Stock Cost / Total Stock Quantity.

flow.title: Material Issue & Pricing Flow
steps: Receive authorized Material Requisition Note
Check chosen inventory valuation method
Calculate unit issue rate from stock lots
Physically issue materials from store
Update Bin Card and Stores Ledger balances

topics.example: With 100 units @ Rs 10 and 100 units @ Rs 12 in stock, FIFO issues 50 units @ Rs 10; Weighted Average issues 50 units @ Rs 11.
remember: FIFO shows higher profit during inflation.
LIFO is NOT permitted under AS 2 / Ind AS 2.
Weighted Average rate updates after each new receipt.
mistakes: Recalculating the weighted average rate on an issue date rather than on the receipt date.

quiz.q: Which inventory pricing method is NOT permitted under Accounting Standard (AS)-2?
quiz.why: AS 2 and Ind AS 2 explicitly prohibit the use of LIFO for financial inventory reporting.

quiz.q: During a period of rising prices (inflation), using the FIFO method results in:
o: Lower profit and lower closing stock valuation
Higher profit and closing stock closer to market value
No effect on reported net profit
quiz.why: FIFO charges older cheaper materials to production (low cost of production, high profit) and leaves newer expensive stock in closing balance.

topics.title: Market Price & Notional Price Valuation Methods
explain: Replacement Price Method values issues at the current market cost needed to repurchase identical material.
Realisable Price Method values issues at the price for which the material could be sold in the market.
Standard Price Method prices issues at a predetermined fixed standard rate, highlighting purchasing cost variances.
Inflated Price Method inflates unit issue rate to absorb inherent normal loss like evaporation or shrinkage.
Re-use Price Method prices scrap or rejected material at a revised rate when repurposed for another job.

flow.title: Inflated Price Calculation
steps: Determine gross cost of purchase lot
Measure original total quantity bought
Deduct expected normal natural loss quantity
Divide gross cost by net usable quantity
Issue materials at the resulting inflated rate

topics.example: Buying 100 liters of solvent for Rs 1,000 where 10 liters naturally evaporate yields an inflated issue price of Rs 1,000 / 90 = Rs 11.11/liter.
remember: Standard Price uses a fixed predetermined rate.
Inflated Price absorbs normal losses like shrinkage or evaporation into good units.
mistakes: Inflating unit issue rates to cover abnormal losses instead of charging them to Costing P&L.

quiz.q: When materials suffer normal weight loss due to natural factors like evaporation, issue rates are adjusted using the:
quiz.why: The Inflated Price Method increases the rate per unit of good units so that normal loss is absorbed into production cost.

quiz.q: The Replacement Price Method values material issues at:
o: Current market price to repurchase the item
quiz.why: Replacement price uses the prevailing market rate required to replace the identical material at the time of issue.

topics.title: Treatment of Material Losses
explain: Normal losses are inherent, unavoidable operational losses absorbed by good units (increases unit cost of good output).
Abnormal losses are avoidable losses charged directly to the Costing Profit and Loss Account.
Waste has no recoverable value; normal waste is absorbed by good units, abnormal waste goes to Costing P&L.
Scrap is incidental residue with small value; realisable value of normal scrap reduces material/overhead cost.
Spoilage refers to damaged units beyond economic repair, disposed of without further processing.
Defectives are imperfect units that can be economically rectified (reworked) into good standard units.
Obsolescence is loss of intrinsic value due to technological shifts; entire loss is debited to Costing P&L.

flow.title: Loss Accounting Treatment
steps: Identify occurrence of material loss
Determine if loss is Normal or Abnormal
If Normal: absorb cost into good production units
If Normal with scrap value: credit sale income to cost
If Abnormal: write off full net loss to Costing P&L

topics.example: Normal evaporation of liquid in boiling is absorbed by output; spilling liquid by dropping a drum is abnormal (debited to P&L).
remember: Normal loss = Cost absorbed by good units.
Abnormal loss = Debited to Costing P&L.
Defectives can be repaired; Spoilage cannot be economically repaired.
mistakes: Absorbing abnormal losses into good units, which artificially inflates the standard product cost.

quiz.q: How is the cost of normal material waste treated in cost accounts?
o: Absorbed by remaining good units produced
quiz.why: Normal waste is inherent to the process, so good production units absorb its cost.

quiz.q: What is the key difference between Spoilage and Defectives?
o: Spoilage has high value, defectives have zero value
Defectives can be economically rectified, spoilage cannot
Spoilage is always abnormal, defectives are always normal
Defectives occur only in store rooms
quiz.why: Defectives can be reconditioned into standard units with rework, whereas spoiled units are discarded without repair.

topics.title: Material Consumption & Accounting Entries
explain: Material consumption occurs when raw materials are physically used in the manufacturing process.
Unique coding systems are assigned to materials and cost centers for accurate direct tracing.
Material Abstract (Material Issue Analysis Sheet) aggregates issue slips to show material consumed per product job.
Indirect material consumption is collected by cost centers and absorbed using overhead absorption rates.
Financial Accounting Formula: Material Consumed = Opening Stock + Purchases - Closing Stock.
Closing stock of materials is valued at cost or Net Realisable Value (NRV), whichever is lower.

flow.title: Material Accounting Workflow
steps: Assign material code and cost center code
Record daily issues via Material Requisitions
Compile weekly Material Abstract Sheet
Charge direct material cost to respective jobs
Calculate period end consumption in Financial Accounts

topics.example: Opening stock Rs 20,000 + Purchases Rs 100,000 - Closing stock Rs 15,000 = Financial Material Consumed Rs 105,000.
remember: Material Abstract summarizes material cost debited to various jobs/products.
Consumption = Opening Stock + Purchases - Closing Stock.
mistakes: Assuming total raw material available for production equals actual material consumed during the period.

quiz.q: A Material Abstract (Material Issue Analysis Sheet) is prepared to:
o: Show a product-wise summary of material consumed
Track physical stock shortages during audit
quiz.why: Material abstract aggregates all requisition notes to show at a glance the value of material consumed for each product.

quiz.q: In financial accounts, raw material consumption is calculated as:
quiz.why: Consumption equals Opening Stock added to Purchases minus Closing Stock.
